refutation.quote: Control: RL minus random rank-8 195 right / 33 cap hits vs RL minus top-8 190 / 90: the accuracy loss is not separable from perturbation, the cap hits are the 8 directions.
refutation.note: The rival's first sentence is 'There is no RL-specific policy of finishing before the cap'. result-51a0e7 (in after.jsonl; hard328, cued, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, v3, one sample) finds that RL's cap-hit avoidance sits in its top-8 singular directions. Removing them from RL gives 90 cap hits, against 33 for a random rank-8 removal and 77 for the base. Adding them at 2x gives 5 cap hits but only 14 right on the base's 77 cap-hit problems. So finishing separates from being right, which is a finishing policy in RL's weights. result-bce075 agrees: RL 'ends the cap hits' of Think-SFT prefixes but 59-65 of 89 become wrong boxed answers. The scope does not exclude this. The rival states its claim generally and itself tests on hard328 (its test 2). Both items do support the rival's measurable claim, that right answers on cap-hit problems follow overall strength: on the 77 base cap hits the counts are rand8 9, k1 15, k8 17, RL 19, which is graded by strength, and RL's stop habit adds no right answers. The item therefore contradicts the rival's wording (no finishing policy), not its rescue-rate numbers. Also read: result-f39ba8 and its comments, result-527fbb, result-b006f5, result-bce075, knowledge-1a0674, knowledge-90431f (via theory and rival text), and the after.jsonl lines on cap hits and Think-SFT.

wins_judgement: Offline the theory has 43 of 44 inside and +35.4 nats, and the replication recomputed all 39 shares exactly. Most of the gain comes from board knowledge more than from the mechanism. (1) The null and RL-cell shares (p5 sharpening null 0.48, +1.78; p2-p6) restate result-f39ba8, which had already posted the same rules on the same per_problem.json: RL 65 = 0/.25/.03/.63/.09, base resample 0/.17/.02/.67/.14. (2) The T 0.6 loop shares (p41 0.52, p49 0.57) were in f39ba8's v3 regrade comment (loops .54). (3) p19, the plain-base answer-statement share of 0.51 (+3.0), follows from knowledge-499152 (166/500 with no answer). Here the theory did earn something by applying R3, because both readers said 0.15-0.18. (4) p48 (+3.0) is a net of 50 inside a hedged interval of 8-52 that the readers' narrow intervals missed. It is a width win, not a mechanism win. The gains that are the mechanism's own are the cross predictions that split loop from budget. The T1 base solves min-p loop-part problems at 0.77 (p57, +0.99) and budget-part problems at 0.29 (p58), and kB>=1 holds on 0.90 of T 0.6 loop problems (p59). I read tests/r6-account/p57.py: it implements the recipe as written (R1-R6 order, rule-A zlib window at line starts, kB from samples 0-2, count = t1_right and not t1_cap_hit). Held-out claims lose -9.9 nats. These are t03/t04 (loop-neuron edit cap hits 47 and 32, predicted 76 and 78), t05/t06 (tokens), and t33: the cued base's per-sample rate on RL-only problems is 0.237, predicted 0.55. t33 cuts against the account's picture of a gap mostly made of sharpening.
rival: Yes, the rival explains the same offline numbers as well. It keeps the theory's rules and attributes the RL budget share (16/27 T1 cap hits fixed, against 7/27 for the null draw) to a strength shift on one axis. The duel is -3.107 nats: loses to rival. metrics_v5 marks 0 separating tests, and tests 1, 2, 4 and 5 carry same_prediction = true. The theory's advocate conceded the matched-difficulty excess: -0.05 on MATH-500 (measured -0.011) and -0.06 on hard328 (measured -0.060). Rival test 3 decides the duel. Think-SFT cue's budget share of the gap against T1 is 0.246 (16/65), inside the rival's [0.12, 0.28] and outside the theory's [0.05, 0.22]. That one test gives -2.14 of the -3.11. I read rivals/r6-account/p3.py and it implements the recipe as written: first row per problem_index, both sides non-null, B right = t1_right and not t1_cap_hit, other right = score_v3 == 1 and not cap_hit, statistic = gap rows with t1_cap_hit / gap. Turn-2 tests 4 (Think-SFT minus RL on the 27 cap hits = 0) and 5 (Think-SFT matched excess -0.034) point the same way but are not separating. The rival's win rests mainly on test 3.

novelty.nearest: Asymmetric truncation: base models hit the per-response token limit far more often than RLVR checkpoints, and 'roughly 0.7 log-odds of ProRL's apparent pass@1 advantage at 8k was simply the base model running out of tokens'. The same paper rejects any single response curve q = T(p) at fixed base difficulty (RLVR acts as a Markov kernel H(q|p)), and in its controlled runs SFT and GRPO differ in slope.
novelty.difference: The paper treats base truncation as an evaluation confound and fits per-prompt kernels. It does not test whether RL rescues base cap hits above its matched-difficulty rate, and it does not compare a reward-free SFT arm with RL on the base's cap-hit problems, which is the rival's claim. Its rejection of a single curve and 2505.07961's 'RL-based models can learn when to stop' (SFT cannot) both stand against the rival's one-axis, no-stopping-policy wording.

account_comparability: The same breakdown of the same cells is already on the board: result-f39ba8 (account run-02/run-03, branch theory), with loop / budget / answer / reliability (= slip + sharpening) / capability (= reach). Its MATH-500 T 1.0 RL cell uses the same per_problem.json T1/T2 rows, grader v3, cue prompt and T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 at cap 16,384, and its shares are the theory's fit to the decimal (65 problems: 0/.25/.03/.63/.09 vs 0/.246/.031/.63/.092). So that cell can be compared and is not new. Its T 0.6 cell is the same base-01 vs step-400 pair at top-p 0.95. It was posted under v1; the v3 regrade in a comment gives loops .54 against the theory's .52, so it compares after regrading. f39ba8's base-resample null (n 42, budget .17, reliability .67) uses a different resample than this theory's null (day1_3 sample 3, n 46, budget .15, slip+sharpening .74), so the two nulls are close but not the same rows. Against its own null, the RL cell's budget share (.246, n 65) sits just above the null's bootstrap interval [0.065, 0.239]. run-03 had found that no part of RL's gap differs from a base-resample null at 90 %, so 'budget exceeds the null' is marginal. The plain-base, top-8, min-p and first-release cells are new in this account.

import_carries_gain.which: The rival imports no published finding. Its numbers come from board items (result-17e25e logit shift, result-5da8a9, knowledge-90431f, result-5de032) and the stored rows. Among the theory's imports, 2510.02611 (temperature reshuffles which problems are solved) and 2504.13837 (sharpening) point the null and sharpening shares in the right direction. The values themselves (p5 0.48, slip 0.26) follow from result-f39ba8's posted base-resample shares and kB counting, not from either paper. 2601.05693 (loop onset) motivates the loop part, but the loop shares (p41, p49) were already on the board in f39ba8.

verdict: weak: the rival beats the theory (-3.107 nats, loses to rival), but its win rests mainly on one test (Think-SFT budget share 0.246, -2.14 of -3.11, with 0 tests marked separating), and result-51a0e7 contradicts its 'no RL-specific policy of finishing' wording. RL's cap-hit avoidance sits in its top-8 directions (90 cap hits with them removed vs 33 for random rank-8), although right answers on cap hits still follow strength, as the rival claims.
